title: Model Value Map for Vertical Buying Committees and Decision Heuristics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Produce a reproducible, verticalized "Model Value Map" (MVM) that converts heterogeneous competitive signals (latency, unit cost, throughput, compliance, license risk, regional availability) into a single score and prescriptive recommendation for the buying committee (SMB product teams, enterprise platform teams, regulated verticals). The MVM will be both an analytical artifact (scorecard + spreadsheet) and a lightweight interactive dashboard used by GTM, sales engineering, and product.
deliverables: Normalized model profile dataset (top 30 public/open model variants + our verified performance profiles)
Per-vertical weighting matrices (SMB, SaaS, FinServ, Health, Gov) with rationale and source citations
Interactive MVM dashboard (Grafana/Looker) with selectable vertical and what-if sliders for latency/cost/SLA sensitivity
PRD/whitepaper describing scoring algorithm, data sources, and decision heuristics for hosted vs dedicated vs private recommendations
Playbook for Sales: short checklist + 3 canned customer pitches mapping MVM outcomes to deployment proposals
methodology_summary: 1) Ingest telemetry and public data: internal token/call volume telemetry, model cards from HF, competitor pricing PDFs, benchmarks, license clauses. 2) Define raw metrics: p50/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/s), per-token list price, quantization support, KMS/HSM availability, geographic region coverage, known license redistribution risk. 3) Normalize and z-score per metric, then apply vertical-specific weights to compute a composite Model Value Score (MVS). 4) Map MVS to a recommended deployment and bundled pricing sensitivity band. 5) Validate via 3 pilot customer interviews and a retrospective run against two months of historical onboarding data.
acceptance_criteria: MVM dataset contains >= 30 model variants with verified latency+cost entries
Dashboard with vertical selector and what-if sliders is accessible to Sales/PM/Eng and documented in PRD
Decision heuristic produces deterministic output for 90% of test cases in a validation set of 60 fictional buyer profiles
At least 3 customer-facing pilots (sales or solutions) validate the recommended deployment type and provide qualitative feedback
Open ENG telemetry gaps are tracked as dependencies and do not block delivery of a first-cut MVM
